name: Storm-1101
iocPatterns: Stolen session cookie usage from non-standard locations
Redirects to benign websites as 'safety' measures
keyCapabilities: MFA bypass via reverse proxy technology
Automated campaign management via Telegram bots
Node.js and PHP-based malicious web applications
Malware development including backdoors and downloaders
recommendedActions: Enforce FIDO2 security keys or certificate-based authentication for high-risk accounts to defeat AiTM.
Implement Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps to detect and flag login events involving stolen session cookies.
Deploy Conditional Access policies in Azure AD based on location, device health, and risk levels.
Enable Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) to reduce the lifespan of valid session tokens.
Monitor login logs for 'impossible travel' or sign-ins from known anonymizer/proxy services.
Implement robust email protection systems capable of identifying and defanging malicious phishing links.
Develop internal communication training specifically regarding AiTM risks and fake identity pages.
Block access to infrastructure identified as belonging to telemetry or proxy networks used by automated kits.
campaignsText: Storm-1101 specializes in a 'malware-as-a-service' and phishing-infrastructure-as-a-service model. Their operations typically begin with the deployment of sophisticated AiTM kits on platforms like exploit.in, followed by high-volume distribution to corporate targets. A notable campaign was executed by DEV-0928 in late 2022/early 2023, which utilized Storm-1101 infrastructure to blast millions of emails. The actor shows an evolving capabilities cycle, adding features like Telegram bot management and advanced CAPTCHA bypasses in the second half of 2022 to meet the demands of higher-tier cybercriminals.
description: Storm-1101 (formerly DEV-1101) is a sophisticated threat actor specialized in developing and distributing high-volume Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing infrastructure. The group provides cybercriminals with tools designed to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) via reverse-proxy technology, supported by automated management features like Telegram bots.
goals: The primary goal of Storm-1101 is economic gain through the sale of phishing kits, subscription services, and premium access to advanced tools. They target broad audiences by providing scalable infrastructure for other threat actors; however, their tooling specifically exploits high-value targets using Microsoft 365 corporate credentials. Target demographics include organizations in critical infrastructure, government, finance, and telecommunications across numerous global regions.
